How Relative Strength Exposes Market Rotation in Real-Time

Sectors and themes constantly rotate under the surface of the market, driven by institutional reallocations. While retail traders chase whatever is flashing green on the surface today, tracking Relative Strength (RS) is your radar for seeing where big money is moving before it becomes obvious.

Here is how following RS helps you map and ride market rotation:

1. Spotting Capital Inflows Early

When institutions rotate out of one sector (like tech) and into another (like energy or financials), they don't do it all at once, they accumulate quietly.

The Tell: 
Even when the broader market is flat or drifting lower, RS leaders in the incoming sector will start bucking the trend. They refuse to pull back, show relative volume expansion on down days, or quickly snap back to highs.

The Edge: 
By monitoring which stocks are holding up or breaking out while everything else stalls, you immediately see where institutional capital is landing.

2. Filtering Out Market Noise

Broader market indices can look messy or range-bound during a rotation phase, trapping traders who only look at the macro view.

The Tell: 
RS strips away the macro noise. If a specific group of stocks is showing persistent relative strength regardless of what the index is doing, you've found the current institutional sweet spot.

The Edge:
 Instead of guessing what sector is cycling in next, you let the price action vote. You follow the names showing structural leadership and trade in alignment with where the heavy sponsorship actually lives.

3. Riding the Wave, Not Chasing the Tail

Rotation isn't a one-day event; it's a multi-week or multi-month trend as capital shifts allocations.

The Tell: 
Once an institutional rotation is underway, the leading RS stocks in that sector form clean continuation patterns (High Tight Flags, volume-backed consolidations, or moving average retests).

The Edge: 
Tracking RS lets you transition smoothly alongside the smart money. As old sectors fade, your watchlist automatically populates with the new leaders driving the next leg of the market cycle.

Don't go for average, go for Elite. Watch the RS leaders, map the rotation, and let the institutional flow guide your entries.

Here is where my heads at heading into the Fed today. 

The 4 scenarios at hand - hike with guidance, no guidance. No hike with guidance, no guidance.

I think we can take no hike out of the equation. Never in history has there been 90% probability of a Fed decision that has gone the other way. So this hike is also likely priced in --- and it's ALL about the speech and outlook. 

If we do see no hike, probably hitting market sell is the best bet as the long end explodes higher on the credibility loss, but don't really see that as a realistic outcome at this point. 

The big thing is Warsh's outlook and the dot plot. 1-2 hikes then done? Or true hiking cycle which would be evidenced by dots showing 3 or more? Think there is virtually zero possibility of a hiking cycle to begin here. This would be worst case scenario in terms of today's reaction. Although, a proper equity selloff with midterms weeks away may lead to an actual Trump TACO in Iran which would be the best outcome for a lasting trend to form. 

What I personally think -- "dovish hike" today. 25bps but Warsh is coy and gives as little information as possible. Market's first reaction is a 'one & done' hike and rips higher in its first move. This short term rip does not get us out of the woods and does not lead to a sustained uptrend, just leads to more chop in my view as there will be no meaningful change to energy/rates. 

But bond positioning is stretched in an oversold condition as the very "obvious" trade which leads me to think a bounce in TLT and therefore equities is afoot. Too many macro headwinds for this to be anything more than a minor positioning bounce in my view though.

Something I don't see many talking about is the upcoming meeting with China this weekend.

Ever hear "sell Rosh Hashana, buy Yom Kippur?" We are in one of the weakest times of the year seasonally here and leave when Yom Kippur kicks off Sunday September 20th.... the same day our meetings with China begin. Trump welcomes XI to the white house a few days later on the 24th. 

CPI came in hot because of energy last week. Under the hood -- CPI less energy had its lowest reading since '22. I think this is the most bullish thing waiting in the wing for us once we get past the obvious headwinds of Iran/energy crisis. If Iran situation is not at the forefront, there is zero reason to hike here. 

What set us off in April that allowed us to ascend higher? China getting Iran to come to the table for a ceasefire. This is what the market needs more than anything else as we immediately see rates and energy plunge in that scenario, kicking off the next great period for the market. 

If you are Trump, with midterms a few weeks away, and the drastic implications that leads to the rest of his presidency.... what is your move? Can't get anything done with congress gridlocked. You're going to pull out all the stops to make sure the market is in great standing as voters head into the booth. Has me thinking he bends the knee in whatever fashion possible to have this energy and rates situation do an about face. 

Lots of speculation in this thought process, we'll see later what we get. Don't feel the need to do much today whatever the news is as --- if there is a lasting trend to come --- there will be nothing but opportunity in the weeks ahead and therefore don't need to trade the whipsaw Fed action in an already unforgiving environment.
